prompt.context: Our client, Unlimited Brands, is a large national retailer with revenues of $12B. Recently they have experienced declines in revenue and profits. They attribute these declines to both changes in consumer tastes as well as decreased investment in several brands due to the desire to preserve capital during the recent downturn. There are two units they are interested in potentially divesting: (1) Fast Fashion — a young women's professional clothing retailer with sales of $500M last year, catering to 18-25 year old women; (2) Devine Design — a fashion forward clothing retailer offering both professional and casual clothing at competitive prices, with sales of $750M last year, catering to 40-55 year old women.
prompt.question: You have been hired to determine the most viable business unit to divest and plan for the separation of the unit from the firm, while maximizing shareholder value. Specifically: (1) What things will the firm need to consider when selling one or more of their business units? (2) Which business unit should Unlimited Brands consider selling to strengthen its cash reserves and deliver the most value to shareholders, and what price should they target for each unit? (3) What ideas would you recommend to Unlimited Brands to strengthen their remaining business?

clarifying_info.a: Yes — a data sheet with historical financials and comparable deal tables will be provided for question 2. No other data will be provided beyond that. Assumptions are acceptable and encouraged.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other business units besides Fast Fashion and Devine Design being considered for divestiture?
clarifying_info.a: No, only these two units are being considered at this time.

framework: Brainstorm divestiture considerations: people/culture, revenue impact, potential buyers, and separation logistics
Value each unit using comparable P/E multiples applied to most recent net income — identify both average and most-recent-multiple scenarios
Assess segment growth trends and revenue trajectory to supplement valuation and support recommendation on which unit to sell
Develop a strengthening strategy for the retained business (pricing, new markets, acquisitions)
Synthesize into a recommendation with clear rationale, risks, and next steps

questions.prompt: What things will the firm need to consider when selling one or more of their business units?
questions.guidance: This is a brainstorming question. Push the candidate to keep generating ideas. Strong answers cover: (1) Culture/People Impact — selling disrupts employees, risks talent attrition, and creates uncertainty across remaining workforce; (2) Impact to Revenue and Earnings — explain earnings impact to shareholders and assess how reduced earnings affect future borrowing capacity; (3) Potential Buyers — identify who would buy, and whether selling to a competitor could strengthen them against Unlimited Brands; (4) Separation logistics — IT systems, store leases, shared mall space, distribution networks, and supplier relationships all require careful planning for a smooth transition.

questions.prompt: Which business unit should Unlimited Brands sell, and what price should they target for each?
questions.guidance: Candidate must walk through all four exhibit tables. Key observations: Fast Fashion revenue and net income have been declining ($625M/$125M in 2009 to $500M/$75M in 2011). Devine Design revenue and net income have been growing ($600M/$90M in 2009 to $675M/$135M in 2011). For valuation, a good answer uses average P/E multiples; a better answer identifies the trend in multiples and uses the most recent comparable deals. Fast Fashion: average P/E = (12+16+20+16+20+12)/6 = 16; most recent comps (Dec 2011) show P/E = 20. Devine Design: average P/E = (10+18+10+14+18+14)/6 = 14; most recent comps (Dec 2011 and Mar 2011) show P/E = 10. Implied valuations — Fast Fashion at 16x: $1.2B; at 20x: $1.5B. Devine Design at 14x: $2.1B; at 10x: $1.35B. Candidate should make a defensible choice: Fast Fashion offers a higher price based on recent multiples and a fast-growing customer segment; Devine Design offers higher price using average multiples and has growing financials despite a declining demographic segment. Either is acceptable if clearly defended.

math.setup: Implied value = P/E multiple x Net Income (most recent year, 2011). Fast Fashion NI 2011 = $75M. Devine Design NI 2011 = $135M (note: table shows $135M for 2011).
steps: Fast Fashion most recent P/E (Dec 2011 comp) = 20
Fast Fashion implied value at avg 16x: 16 x $75M = $1,200M = $1.2B
Fast Fashion implied value at recent 20x: 20 x $75M = $1,500M = $1.5B
Devine Design most recent P/E (Dec 2011 comp) = 10
Devine Design implied value at avg 14x: 14 x $135M = $1,890M ≈ $1.9B (casebook rounds to $2.1B using $150M NI estimate — note discrepancy; casebook states $150M)
Devine Design implied value at recent 10x: 10 x $135M = $1,350M = $1.35B
math.answer: Fast Fashion: ~$1.2B (avg multiple) to ~$1.5B (recent multiple). Devine Design: ~$1.35B (recent multiple) to ~$2.1B (avg multiple, per casebook using ~$150M NI).

questions.prompt: What ideas would you recommend to Unlimited Brands to strengthen their remaining business?
questions.guidance: This is a sell-additional-work / growth strategy question. Strong answers include: (1) Improved Pricing — examine current pricing structure to maximize price realization; develop a smarter promotion strategy (when to promote, who to target, what to promote); (2) New Market Opportunities — target new customer segments or cross-sell new product categories to existing customers; (3) Acquisitions — use divestiture proceeds to acquire a smaller player in a complementary space to enhance the brand portfolio.

brainstorming.prompt: What things will the firm need to consider when selling one or more of their business units?

categories.name: Culture and People
ideas: Risk of talent attrition as employees fear further sell-offs
Disruption to morale across the broader organization
Importance of retaining key leaders of the divested unit through transition

categories.name: Revenue and Earnings Impact
ideas: Explaining reduced consolidated earnings to shareholders
Potential impact on credit ratings and borrowing capacity

categories.name: Potential Buyers
ideas: Assess whether selling to a direct competitor would strengthen them at Unlimited Brands' expense
Consider international buyers to avoid competitive risk

categories.name: Separation Logistics
ideas: IT systems separation and data migration
Shared store or mall footprint — lease renegotiation
Distribution center and supply chain disentanglement
Day 1 and Day 2 operational readiness plans

recommendation: Recommend selling Fast Fashion based on the most recent P/E comparable multiple of 20x, implying a price of ~$1.5B — the highest achievable value — given its fast-growing 18-25 customer segment and recent upward trend in comparable deal multiples; alternatively, recommend selling Devine Design at the average multiple of ~14x for ~$1.9-2.1B if maximizing absolute proceeds is the priority, given its growing revenue and profit trajectory
Either choice is defensible — the key is committing to one unit, stating the valuation rationale, and addressing the strategic implications of that choice
risks: Selling to a competitor who uses the acquired brand to gain market share against Unlimited Brands
Mispricing the asset — using wrong multiples leads to leaving value on the table or a failed sale process
Losing key management talent to attrition during the sale process, reducing the attractiveness of the divested unit to buyers
next_steps: Identify and shortlist potential strategic and financial buyers
Engage investment bank to run a formal sale process and determine final price guidance
Establish Day 1 and Day 2 separation plans covering IT, operations, supply chain, and store transitions
Use proceeds to fund growth initiatives (acquisitions, new markets, pricing improvements) in the retained business
